Definition: probably from the base of G1150; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman:--Damaris.
BiblicalUsage: Damaris is named once, among the few who believed when Paul spoke in Athens. Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris are the named fruit of a sermon most of the city mocked.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Damaris matters because she shows that the gospel finds its hearers even in the hardest ground: a few believed, and Luke bothered to name them.
